summary: Feed s121_double is degraded: 70.6% of traffic is VXLAN-encapsulated and opaque to the SIEM, and 2.9% of frames exceed the SIEM's 1518-byte MTU and are dropped by its NIC.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker is forwarding VXLAN-encapsulated traffic (1428/2023 frames) without stripping the outer header. The SIEM receives only outer VXLAN/UDP/IP and cannot see inner Ethernet/IP/TCP headers.
findings.impact_on_tool: SIEM is blind to 70.6% of inner flows - cannot parse inner 5-tuple, apply correlation rules, or detect lateral movement hidden inside VXLAN. Detection coverage severely reduced.

recommended_fix.why: Strip VXLAN header on the packet broker and forward only the inner packet so the SIEM can parse and correlate the original traffic without needing tunnel decapsulation.

findings.root_cause: 58 frames (2.9%) are larger than the SIEM's 1518-byte port MTU, up to 8108 bytes. Likely jumbo frames and VXLAN overhead pushing frames over the limit; the SIEM NIC drops oversize frames on ingress.
findings.impact_on_tool: SIEM loses ~2.9% of traffic completely due to NIC drops, creating gaps in logging and alerting. Even though SIEM needs_full_payload=false, it receives nothing for those frames.

recommended_fix.why: Configure packet broker to slice/trim frames to 1518 bytes (or less) before delivery. SIEM does not need full payload, so slicing preserves headers for detection while preventing NIC drops.
